look_here_first: LOW MAT of small smooth-edged KIDNEY-SHAPED leaves, each on a long upright petiole from a creeping/rooting stem. Follow the stem: leaves are ALTERNATE, not opposite. Turn leaves over to find a solitary tiny PALE GREEN or CREAM five-lobed flower, much shorter-stalked than the leaves. If distinguishing from another Dichondra, check the fruiting stalk: usually STRAIGHT or barely bent and the FIVE persistent sepals LONGER than the little two-lobed capsule. Do NOT rely on round leaves alone.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Prostrate stolon-forming perennial herb only a few cm high; many rounded kidney-shaped leaves on ascending petioles create the visual mat.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaves ALTERNATE along creeping stolons; blades simple, kidney-shaped (reniform), cleft/notched at the base, with an ENTIRE (untoothed) margin.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Several main PALMATE veins radiate from the notch/petiole junction rather than one single midrib.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Tiny solitary flower sits in a leaf axil usually below the leaf canopy; pale green/cream corolla with five short lobes, not a yellow composite head.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Green CALYX of five separate often hairy sepals persists as petals disappear and enlarges with maturing fruit.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Fruit matures into a tiny distinctly two-lobed dry capsule; in D. carolinensis its persistent sepals are generally noticeably longer than the capsule.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: To separate close Dichondra look-alikes, a roughly straight/nonnodding pedicel in fruit is more useful than whether one leaf looks bigger or greener.

key_traits.label: Growth habit
key_traits.text: Mat-forming or loose creeping cover, with subterranean/at-surface slender stolons rooting at nodes, leafy tips standing to approximately 5 cm in the central-Texas detailed specimen treatment. Often hidden amongst grass and leaf litter.

key_traits.label: Life cycle
key_traits.text: Perennial herb, creeping and rooting along stolons.

key_traits.label: Stem
key_traits.text: Slender runners at or just beneath soil surface, occasional aboveground red-green hairy stems; local UT treatment notes two-armed strigose hairs on green organs, often not visible without a hand lens.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Helically ALTERNATE—one petiolate leaf per node, NOT true opposite pairs. Dense runners can make nearby petioles appear paired; physically trace one stem.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Simple, kidney-shaped to suborbicular; rounded or slightly indented tip, deeply cordate/notched petiole base, smooth/ENTIRE margins, variable minute hairs. UT local specimens approximately 10–23 mm long by 10–30 mm wide; FNA broader 3–25 by 6–30 mm including extremes.

key_traits.label: Leaf venation
key_traits.text: Palmate, several major veins (UT reports commonly 3, 5, or 7) diverging from the petiole base; veins conspicuous on underside when leaf is flipped.

key_traits.label: Petiole
key_traits.text: Long, upright/slightly oblique leaf stalk: FNA commonly 10–50 mm, sometimes to 105 mm; much longer than tiny flower stalk in typical specimens. Petiole is attached at the BASE notch, not centrally on the leaf blade.
